key_insight: Separating radar-state prediction from language alignment improves radar-to-text retrieval without degrading continuous physical-state estimates.
engineering_relevance: Privacy-preserving mmWave sensing could support motion and scene monitoring through darkness, smoke, and walls, although fracture or material-damage assessment is not demonstrated.
method: Dual-scale RF encoder and ~3% LoRA-adapted LLM predict physical states 3 seconds ahead.
Two-step EMA-JEPA training combines denoising, rollout, and sample-axis Batch-VICReg.
A separate stop-gradient alignment head maps frozen physical representations to text with false-negative masking.
evidence_signal: On 4,541 radar windows across three domains against 10 baselines, head-only alignment increased radar-to-text R@10 from 5.95% to 15.01% while preserving physical readouts, including 3.37° blackout torso-tilt error at +3 seconds.
watch_item: Retrieval R@10 remains 15.01%, and transfer beyond the evaluated radar domains—including structural damage sensing—requires validation.
paper_title: PhysRF-WorldJEPA: Transforming Heterogeneous Large Language Models into Manifold-Decoupled Millimeter-Wave Radar World Models
